title: Shopify alternative in India: GoCommerce vs Shopify
description: Shopify India vs GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce: the fee every Indian store pays without Shopify Payments, GST, cash on delivery and Razorpay.
ogDescription: No Shopify Payments in India means a fee on every prepaid order. What that takes by plan, against running GoCommerce yourself or hosting it on kitcommerce.store.
h1: Shopify alternative in India: GoCommerce vs Shopify
tagline: In India, Shopify charges a plan and a cut of every prepaid order.
lede: Shopify Payments is not offered in India, so an Indian store takes online payments through a third-party gateway such as Razorpay — and Shopify adds its own fee of 2%, 1% or 0.6% of each of those orders, by plan, on top of what the gateway charges. Run GoCommerce yourself and it talks to Razorpay directly, with the gateway’s charge the only one per order. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale, {plusGst}.

Shopify’s fee on a prepaid order
Basic 2%, Grow 1%, Advanced 0.6%, Plus 0.2% — worked out on the order total, tax and shipping included. Shopify Payments would waive it, and India does not have it.
None when you run it yourself: GoCommerce adds nothing to the cost of an order. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale, {plusGst}.
Cash on delivery
A manual payment method, and Shopify’s help centre says the fee does not apply to it.
Built into the core: “cod” is the default payment method, with nothing to install.
Razorpay
Connected as a third-party provider: Razorpay’s own charge, then Shopify’s fee on the same order.
The payments-razorpay module calls Razorpay’s API directly. Razorpay lists 2% + GST as its standard rate, UPI included, and on a store you run yourself that is the whole payment cost.
Features tied to Shopify Payments
Shopify’s plan table marks showing prices in local currencies and accepting local payment methods through Markets as requiring Shopify Payments.
No feature waits on a particular gateway: price lists, discounts and channels behave the same whichever payment module you import.
Indian couriers
Shopify’s plan table lists live third-party shipping rates at checkout from Advanced upward.
Shiprocket, Delhivery and NimbusPost modules book shipments. The India Post module records the consignment number from the counter receipt, because India Post publishes no booking API.
Order SMS
Pay-per-send SMS campaigns sit in every plan’s marketing tools.
The MSG91 module texts customers when an order is placed, paid, shipped, delivered or cancelled, sent as DLT-registered templates as Indian rules require.
GST on the platform’s bill
Charged on Shopify’s fees to a store in India unless you register your GSTIN; GST on invoices issued before you do cannot be reversed.
No platform bill to tax when you run it yourself. Your host’s invoice carries whatever GST it charges.
GST invoices for your orders
Shopify says it does not create GST-compliant bills, and points to a local invoicing service or an App Store app.
The invoices module gives every paid order a numbered invoice and prints your GSTIN, but shows no CGST, SGST or IGST split.
Trying it
3 days free, then a reduced price for the first 3 months on most plans.
Free for as long as you like: the one-command Docker stack runs the API and admin on your own machine.
Plus in India
A one- or three-year term, plus 0.2% of every order a third-party gateway takes — which, here, is every prepaid one.
The same software as any other GoCommerce store. The Shopify Plus comparison covers that side in full.

faq.q: Is Shopify Payments available in India?
faq.a: No. India is not on Shopify’s list of countries where Shopify Payments is supported, so an Indian store takes online payments through a third-party provider such as Razorpay, and Shopify charges its third-party transaction fee on those orders: 2%, 1% or 0.6% on Basic, Grow and Advanced, and 0.2% on Plus.

faq.q: Does Shopify charge its fee on cash-on-delivery orders?
faq.a: No. Shopify’s help centre lists manual payment methods — cash on delivery, bank deposits, cheques — among the payments the fee does not apply to, along with POS orders. It does apply to store credit and gift card payments on stores created on or after 12 May 2025.

faq.q: Does Shopify add GST to its bill?
faq.a: Yes, for a store located in India, unless you give Shopify your GSTIN. Shopify’s help centre says the exemption applies only to invoices issued after you submit it, and GST already charged on earlier invoices cannot be reversed or refunded.

faq.q: Which Shopify plan is cheapest for an Indian store?
faq.a: It depends on prepaid sales. Each step up costs more a month and takes a smaller cut of each prepaid order: 2% on Basic, 1% on Grow, 0.6% on Advanced. A store with small prepaid sales pays least on Basic, and the higher plans pay off only as prepaid sales grow — before GST, and before the gateway’s own charge.

faq.q: Can I have a GoCommerce store without running a server?
faq.a: Yes. A store hosted on kitcommerce.store pays {hostedFee} of each successful sale, {plusGst}. Running GoCommerce yourself stays free, and then the gateway’s charge is the only cost per order.

faq.q: What does GoCommerce use for payments and shipping in India?
faq.a: Razorpay through the payments-razorpay module, and cash on delivery in the core. Shipments are booked through the Shiprocket, Delhivery and NimbusPost modules, and the India Post module records consignment numbers. Order SMS go out through MSG91 as DLT-registered templates. Each module is compiled in only if you import it.

Partly. The invoices module gives every paid order a numbered invoice in a gapless sequence and prints your GSTIN, but it shows no tax breakdown — no HSN codes, no CGST, SGST or IGST. Shopify says it does not create GST-compliant bills either, and points merchants to an invoicing app or service.
